replies.text:
Step 2 checks:

- Automated abuse reachable (brute force / flooding / mass sign-up / scraping): design has a public, unauthenticated flow — "The QR code holds the customer id and is generated on the phone, so it works offline" with `"auth":false`, `"exposure":"public"`. Covered by listed threats 5 (flooding) and 2 (bulk personal-data retrieval / id probing).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing content other people supply: design mentions only "cashiers scan at the till to add points" — no privileged screen rendering customer-supplied content. Not present in design.
- Deleting / refunding / approving / moving money or goods with no record of who did it: present — "Points can be swapped for free products in the app." Goods leave the business on redemption, and the listed repudiation threat 6 is scoped to accrual ("no evidence tying a scan to a specific app install or a specific till receipt"), not to who authorised the redemption of goods. Not covered.
- Personal/financial/account documents or pages cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design names no document, PDF or page served over HTTP. Not present in design.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails, headers or another system: design names no export, email or log sink. Not present in design.
- Single-reviewer threats reviewed: replay of a static screenshot (1, 5, 9) and bot generation across guessed ids (7, 8) are the same unsigned-id weakness as listed threat 1; cashier crediting unlimited points (11) is the same till-trust weakness as listed threat 4; id enumeration (3, 6, 10) falls under listed threat 2; unverified accrual before redemption (2) falls under listed threat 3. Only redemption accountability (12, partly) is a distinct, design-stated gap.

    "components": ["mobile app", "QR code generator (on-device)", "till scanner / cashier client", "loyalty points service", "redemption (free products)"],
    "dataStores": ["customer loyalty accounts / point balances"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["phone to till", "till to loyalty service", "app to loyalty service"],

  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Redeeming points for free products leaves no record of who authorised the handover",
      "scenario": "Redemption happens in the app with nothing in the design recording who redeemed, on which install, or which goods were handed over. A customer who swaps points for free products can later claim the redemption was never made and demand the balance back, and staff colluding with customers can convert balances into goods with no trail to review. Because the only stated record path is the offline-generated code, the business cannot reconstruct which redemptions were genuine, so goods walk out and losses go undetected.",
      "component": "Redemption in mobile app / loyalty points service",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Points can be swapped for free products in the app." },
        { "quote": "The QR code holds the customer id and is generated on the phone, so it works offline." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "When someone trades points for free goods, nothing records who did it or what they took, so people can deny redemptions and abuse goes unnoticed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record every points redemption with actor and goods",
        "given": "a customer swaps loyalty points for a free product in the app",
        "when": "the redemption is accepted by the loyalty service",
        "then": "the service writes an immutable record of the customer id, device/app install, timestamp, points deducted and product granted, and that record is retained and reviewable for dispute and fraud investigation"
      }
    }
  ]
}
